html:
The Athabasca oil sands in northern Alberta hold one of the largest oil reserves in the world, in sand soaked with thick bitumen. Commercial production began in 1967 at the Great Canadian Oil Sands plant near Fort McMurray.

Bitumen is mined in vast open pits or heated underground so it can flow. The Cree had used it to seal canoes long before. High oil prices from the 2000s brought a boom and made Canada one of the largest oil producers and the main supplier of oil to the United States.

The sands are costly to work and emit more greenhouse gas than most oil. The tailings ponds and pollution concern First Nations downstream, such as the Dene and Cree of Fort Chipewyan. Pipelines to carry the oil, such as Keystone XL, became battles over climate change.
